correctness.rationale: The section at fixed hub t is exactly (c_r-t^r)^m for t<=1/2 and (1-t)^(rm) above, from disjoint high-coordinate caps. The true stable polytope has simplex fibers with total volume (r!)^(-m)/(rm+1). The scaled fractional integral converges by the integrable dominating function exp(-u^r/c_r), yielding its gamma normalization and the hub density. The true hub coordinate has exact Beta(1,rm+1) law. Separately run check.py verified 24 exact/quadrature, 8 independent convex hull, 12 volume-limit and 9 CDF comparisons; they are corroboration only. No assertion about variable r is made.

originality.rationale: The new single theorem gives a fixed-clique-size hub-coordinate probability law, an explicit m^(-1/r) versus m^(-1) concentration-scale distinction, and a sharp polynomial amplification of the relaxation/integral volume ratio. Steingrimsson (1994) gives an all-graph finite volume recursion, so finite numerical volumes are not treated as independent novelty. Hamano–Hibi–Ohsugi (2016) prove Ehrhart and ring results for the same fractional-polytope class without a windmill hub-coordinate law. Okada–Tsuchiya (2020) discuss underlying poset polytopes and enriched transfers without this relaxation phenomenon. Actual indexed searches found no mathematically implying statement; less-indexed overlap remains a risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed study of uniform points in vertex-packing polytopes or a solved windmill deletion recurrence could contain an equivalent asymptotic marginal.
Steingrimsson already covers general finite-volume recursion, so formula-for-individual-m novelty is not claimed; the new value requires the localization comparison.
No independent bibliographic or mathematical audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The motivating geometry is the relaxation gap of chain polytopes of common-hub clique sums. The shared vertex drives a nontrivial power-law excess in full-dimensional volume and forces m^(-1/r) concentration in the relaxation versus m^(-1) in the true chain polytope; for friendship graphs the √m excess is present despite each non-hub block having zero local integrality gap. The precise hub marginal and polynomial factor describe a natural robust infinite family, not a numerical table or routine graph parameter substitution.
